vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: sparki-video-editor
Version: 1.0.5

The sparki-video-editor skill is a legitimate CLI tool and agent instruction set for interacting with the Sparki AI video editing service. It facilitates video uploads, project management, and result downloads via the agent-api.sparki.io endpoint. The code in cli.py and client.py follows standard practices for API interaction, and the instructions in SKILL.md are appropriately scoped to guide the AI agent through the service's specific multi-step workflow without attempting to exfiltrate sensitive data or execute unauthorized commands.

llm.summary: The skill's code, runtime instructions, and requested access are consistent with an AI video-editing CLI that uses a Sparki API key and the Sparki backend; nothing in the package suggests unrelated credential requests, suspicious network endpoints, or hidden exfiltration.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (AI video editing) align with the code and declared primaryEnv (SPARKI_API_KEY). The CLI implements upload, edit, status, download, and history commands and targets the declared domain (agent-api.sparki.io). The only mildly unexpected item is the declared required binary 'uv' in metadata; the Python CLI itself doesn't appear to need an external 'uv' runtime to function, but 'uv' may be a platform helper for syncing skills rather than a capability mismatch.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to check/save an API key, offer upload links, accept local file paths or Telegram mini-app uploads, and run the sparki CLI commands. The instructions limit file access to local paths and explicitly restrict direct Telegram attachments. The commands and file paths referenced (reading files from $CWD, writing config and workspace under ~/.openclaw) match the code's behavior. There are no instructions to read unrelated system files or to transmit data to endpoints other than the Sparki backend.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No extract/download-from-URL install spec is present (lower risk). The SKILL.md contains an 'install' fragment that runs 'uv sync', but there's no platform-level install script that fetches arbitrary code; the package includes local Python sources and a pyproject listing dependencies (typer, httpx, pydantic). If the platform will execute this Python code, those dependencies must be available — the skill does not itself fetch third-party packages from untrusted URLs. Overall installation risk is low, but the role of the 'uv' binary could use clarification.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests a single primary credential (SPARKI_API_KEY) which is required to call the Sparki API; the code also optionally respects SPARKI_UPLOAD_TG_LINK for the Telegram upload URL. No unrelated secrets or cloud credentials are requested. The skill writes a local config file (~/.openclaw/config/sparki.json) to store the API key and tracks history under the same directory — this behavior is documented and expected.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false (no forced global inclusion). The skill requests read access to the current working directory and write access to its own config and workspace directories — these are proportional to uploading and downloading video files. The skill does not request system-wide settings or other skills' credentials.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: it needs a Sparki API key and will contact agent-api.sparki.io to upload/process videos. Before installing, confirm where you'll obtain the SPARKI_API_KEY (use an official Sparki source), and be comfortable that the skill will save that key to ~/.openclaw/config/sparki.json. Note the skill will read files from your current working directory and write edited videos to ~/.openclaw/workspace/sparki/videos — avoid running it from folders with sensitive files. The metadata asks for a 'uv' binary; ask the publisher what 'uv' does in your environment if you don't recognize it. If you plan to run the code locally, ensure Python 3.11+ and the listed dependencies (typer, httpx, pydantic) are provided by a trusted runtime. Finally, avoid uploading sensitive private videos to the remote service unless you accept the privacy implications.
